title: Finite relation data and descent for an injective module map
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $N$ an $A$-module, $M$ a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and $u:N\to M$ an injective $A$-linear map. There exist natural numbers $a,b$ and $A$-linear maps $d:A^b\to A^a$, $\alpha:A^a\to M$, $\beta:A^b\to N$ such that $u\beta=\alpha d$ and, for every $A$-linear $\gamma:A^a\to N$, the equality $\beta=\gamma d$ implies existence of an $A$-linear $v:M\to N$ with $vu=\mathrm{id}_N$.

source.place: Tag 02HO, proof: the finite free presentation and splitting criterion; adapted to a free presentation of M

proof.text: Choose a finite free surjection $\alpha:A^a\to M$. Set $K=\alpha^{-1}(u(N))$. This submodule of a finite free module is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. Choose a finite free surjection $\delta:A^b\to K$ and let $d$ be its composite with inclusion.
The injective map $u$ identifies $N$ with $u(N)$. Compose its inverse with $\alpha d$ to obtain $\beta$ with $u\beta=\alpha d$.

If $\beta=\gamma d$, then $\gamma$ vanishes on $\ker\alpha$: write $x=d(y)$ using surjectivity onto $K$; $u\beta(y)=\alpha(x)=0$ gives $\beta(y)=0$. Descend $\gamma$ to $v:M\to N$ through the first isomorphism theorem. Given $n$, choose $x$ with $\alpha(x)=u(n)$ and write $x=d(y)$. Injectivity gives $\beta(y)=n$, hence $v(u(n))=\gamma(x)=\beta(y)=n$.

lean.statement: theorem LinearMap.exists_finite_relation_splitting_data {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {N : Type v} [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M] (u : N →ₗ[A] M) (hu : Function.Injective u) : ∃ (a b : ℕ) (d : (Fin b → A) →ₗ[A] (Fin a → A)) (α : (Fin a → A) →ₗ[A] M) (β : (Fin b → A) →ₗ[A] N), u.comp β = α.comp d ∧ (∀ γ : (Fin a → A) →ₗ[A] N, β = γ.comp d → ∃ v : M →ₗ[A] N, v.comp u = LinearMap.id)
